about: READ-ONLY: discover the largest whole-GiB expansion one run can currently admit for an explicit instance namespace/PVC, through infra/forge/expand-instance-volume.sh --plan-largest (PARTIAL backlog53c8cb72). Reads the same claim, StorageClass, Longhorn volume, replica/node lists and settings as the existing explicit-size plan, refuses incomplete or ambiguous identities and noninteger/unsafe numeric facts, and uses the existing shared Longhorn admission arithmetic. Counts ALL assigned replicas on each disk; selects the minimum of current physical and scheduling-ledger fit, 2x the current capacity and the script's100GiB ceiling. Prints exactly one JSON proposal with verb=plan-an-instance-volume-expansion, explicit args=[namespace,pvc,resolved-size], the ordinary expansion plan and its plan_sha256; the hash also rides stderr. WHEN NO GROWTH FITS (design ada8f698, option A, David 2026-10-07): at the script's ceiling it refuses, since no replica move changes a ceiling; otherwise a replica disk is what binds, and it asks infra/forge/move-volume-replica.sh --plan-decisive <volume> <namespace> <pvc> the one further question — would EXACTLY ONE replica move free the volume? That read holds the volume to the claim, re-reads Longhorn through the same complete-list and exact-integer guards, runs every bound plan-a-volume-replica-move runs (attached, healthy, every declared replica healthy and active one per node, hard anti-affinity, no data locality, no auto-balance, no eviction, every disk the new replica can land on passing the ledger and the live placement and next-growth checks), requires that some replica disk is short of the next growth and that the volume holds no more replicas than the retirement floor (above it, retiring is as admissible as moving, and the choice is a person's), and judges each replica as the source: eligible only when every REMAINING replica disk admits the projected growth by the plan's own ledger and live sums. Exactly one eligible replica prints one JSON proposal with verb=plan-a-volume-replica-move, args=[volume,replica], target=[namespace,pvc], that replica's ordinary move plan and its plan_sha256; none or several refuse (exit 78) naming every candidate, and an unreadable or partial read is CANNOT ANSWER (exit 1). It selects on evidence or not at all, never by listing order, and it moves no replica: from that proposal the dispatcher files only the read-only plan-a-volume-replica-move request, and move-volume-replica stays a request a person files and David's passkey signs. This is argument discovery, not automatic request filing, approval or execution. A later request must freeze the explicit proposal arguments; the unchanged expand-instance-volume mutation still requires David's passkey-signed exact plan hash and rechecks live conditions. No dynamic auto size reaches the mutation. Discovery may change as live headroom changes; the resolved explicit-size plan excludes live free-space values so admissible changes leave its approval hash unchanged. Ranked or multi-step movement (the design's option B) is not built. No credential or cluster write. Timeout 240: a no-growth answer reads the cluster twice.
